A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation and mitigation experiments, human evaluation, robustness analyses and intent-detection results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds evaluator comparisons, unseen-character validation, human assessment of consistency and statistical tests.

M1.justification: The candidate-generation and ranking algorithms, prompt rewriting, negative-prompt combinations, and DETECT/CONS computations remain unchanged. Additional evaluator validation and clarification of the simulated rewriting pipeline do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds evaluator-generalization testing on 50 character identities outside the original 50-character set. This extends character coverage for evaluator validation; the main generation tasks, original character collection and training-corpus analyses are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 adds Claude Sonnet and Llava-34b alongside GPT-4V in evaluator comparisons. Table 7 compares GPT-4V and Claude Sonnet on unseen characters. Existing generation, ranking and mitigation comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New validation protocols compare detector prompts with versus without character names and evaluate CONS against majority-vote binary author annotations using AUROC. Existing generation configurations and the 200-image, six-author detector-validation protocol are unchanged; the latter is relocated to Appendix C.3.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3–C.4 substantially expand measurement validation through evaluator-model and prompt-format ablations, generalization tests on unseen characters, and the first human validation of CONS. The earlier detector-human study and existing mitigation, spelling-robustness and embedding analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: New Table 3 reports one-tailed significance tests at alpha = 0.05 for adding negative prompts under two prompting conditions. Three-run means and standard deviations were already reported in v1 and remain unchanged; no increase in run counts is stated.

E6.justification: New results include evaluator-comparison scores, GPT-4V accuracy of 80% and kappa of 0.52 on unseen characters, CONS-human AUROC of 0.82, and t-values of 8.59 and 6.51. Existing mitigation results in Tables 1–2 and the matched supplementary result tables are unchanged; these additions do not demonstrate improved mitigation performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of DETECT and CONS and the ranking algorithms are retained. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a dual-metric evaluation framework, indirect-anchor discovery, insufficient protection from rewriting alone, and benefits from combining rewriting with negative prompts. Removing COPYCAT branding and reorganizing the research questions do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly cautions that mitigation sufficiency depends on jurisdiction and its metrics are not universal optimization targets. Appendix C.6 acknowledges that the extracted DALL·E prompt may only approximate production behavior. Section 7 also newly argues that evaluator errors do not alter method rankings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct code-repository link and a reproducibility statement reporting supplementary code, data and instructions. Appendix C.6 expands prompt-extraction provenance and describes manual checks. The ethics statement discusses possible request-only sharing of some images; existing hardware, timing and generation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on copyright-unlearning benchmarks, concept erasure, language-model copyright issues and prompt extraction, while dropping references including Chin et al. and the GPT-4 technical report. It elaborates the distinction from attack and unlearning research without fundamentally changing its inference-time mitigation positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and evaluation-framework exposition are extensively rewritten. Character curation is deemphasized in the main text, the original human-evaluation appendix is integrated into C.3, and ethics and reproducibility statements are added. Some new editorial defects remain, including malformed citations and an unfinished Appendix A sentence.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3, 6 and 7 and adopts the ICLR layout, with revised captions and repositioned displays. Existing figures retain their images and plotted findings; several are renumbered or resized rather than replaced with new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens confidence in the evaluation through alternative-detector comparisons, unseen-character checks and human validation of CONS, which v1 lacked. Statistical testing and clearer legal and simulation qualifications also help. The main findings remain unchanged, while sparse details for the new annotation studies and new citation/prose errors limit the overall gain.
